title: Preferring the small group; poor big-band arrangements; Rudy Powell's charts
summary: He preferred the small group because big-band parts were demanding and the arrangements bad; the better ones came from an unpaid bandmate, Rudy Powell.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you enjoy playing the big band, or did you prefer the small group?
Well, I -- I preferred the small group, because you know, let's face it, you don't have all those big
There's more opportunity for you in a small group, right?

Yeah, I mean you know. You play, open up, open up three or four, five sheets of paper, and you've got to read it all, hit all those high notes, you know, and all that mess up, for what? You know. And most times our arrangements stunk.
You know. I mean they were lousy.
Who wrote them? Do you know?
Yes, I did. I did know that, and I want to be fair to this guy, but man, some of our arrangements were lousy.
(Laughs) well, it's usually a guy who's close by who did not get paid. Would you believe that? Who wrote the better ones.

Well now, I'm going to tell you a little story. When I went in the group I was -- I'll tell you about Rudy Powell. Rudy Powell played clarinet, played clarinet and alto saxophone (or) a lot of Fats' things. And I think

a lot of people looked on that knows is that him, you know, when they shouldn't have, because Rudy -- he's a great cat. Did some fine things, you know? When he came in the band, even Sedric was there, and he's sitting there playing, you know. Rudy made some arrangements --
